purpose: R4H-L evidence for `grapt-location`. QL01-QL09 each name one load-bearing behaviour of the bind boundary, the exact source edit that removes it, and the witness that must turn red once it is gone. QL10-QL15 do the same for the acceptance corpus itself: cold review R1 turned three corpus corruptions green against a validator that was not fail-closed, so each of those classes - contract identity, schema version, executable-owner binding, declared target, terminal-bind outcome and refusal classification - now carries a row that corrupts the fixture and must turn the corpus owner red. A witness that stays green under its own mutation attributes nothing. QL16-QL21 close the R1 CLOSURE survivor: nested bind-plan and receipt-observation payloads are typed by shape, by value and against the other records of their own scenario, with wrong-host, wrong-port, zero-port, plan-side and mismatched-record controls. QL23-QL24 witness the R4H-H accept seam: the admitted connection reports the observed local address and never confuses it with the peer. QL25 witnesses the dependency-direction gate against the REAL manifest using grapt-types, which exists at this base; the deferred grapt-api form would compile-kill instead of scoring.
isolation: Every mutation is applied inside its own disposable git worktree checked out at the exact candidate commit. No mutant is ever written into the calling worktree, so there is no restore step that could leave a stale build behind.
scope_note: The two trybuild probes carry no QL row on purpose. `Fixed(NonZeroU16)` and the absent `Clone` on `BoundListener` are compile-time seams: removing either does not produce a program that compiles and fails a test, it produces a program in which the probe compiles. Those laws are witnessed by requiredness in tests/compile_fail.rs, and inventing a mutation row for them would be a duplicate receipt for evidence the harness cannot actually score. QL01 and QL02 are separated deliberately: QL01 makes the receipt echo the request, which only an ephemeral plan can detect, while QL02 turns the ephemeral intent into the oracle's 4096 search base, which only a second concurrent bind can detect. Neither witness covers the other.
